result.title: Data-Scarce, Multi-Granular, Multimodal: Benchmark Design for Biosynthetic Gene Clusters
result.comment: 43 pages, including references and appendices. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations and Datasets Track)
result.summary: Biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) are co-located genes that encode the biosynthesis of specialized metabolites, an important source of antibiotics, anticancer agents, immunosuppressants, and agricultural bioactives. Deep learning, particularly self-supervised foundation models, has spurred interest in BGC sequence modeling, but evaluation has lagged behind: existing benchmarks often rely on coarse classification over small curated datasets, providing limited discrimination among models and insight into downstream utility. We propose a benchmark-design framework in which an informative benchmark should be discriminative, separating models with statistical confidence, and applicable, spanning scientifically meaningful tasks under different levels of generalization. We instantiate this framework as BGC-Bench, which derives five tasks from MIBiG, ranging from A-domain substrate prediction to BGC-molecule retrieval, evaluates them under genotype- and phenotype-shift splits, includes an active-learning setting for label-scarce discovery, and is easily extensible to new tasks and encoders. BGCs further provide a shared testbed across granularities and modalities: BGC-Bench compares twelve encoders on nucleotide, amino-acid, or Pfam-domain sequences, including compositional baselines for each input type, and combines BGC and chemical encoders for cross-modal retrieval. No single representation dominates: the best granularity depends on the biological scale of the task, and pretrained encoders do not consistently outperform other representations across tasks and splits. Active-learning experiments show that most tasks remain data-limited, encoder rankings change with labeling budget, and acquisition strategies yield modest gains. These results show that BGC model evaluation requires task-diverse, shift-aware benchmarks, and the framework can be generalized to benchmark design beyond BGCs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对生物合成基因簇（BGC）建模提出基准设计框架，要求评测具备判别性与任务适用性，并据此构建 BGC-Bench：从 MIBiG 派生五个任务，在基因型与表型偏移划分下比较十二种核苷酸、氨基酸、Pfam 域编码器及跨模态检索，并加入标签稀缺的主动学习设置。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“无单一表示占优、最佳粒度随任务尺度变化”及跨模态检索、标签预算影响排名的发现，可能为 LVR 中视觉/语言表示的粒度选择、证据筛选与评价划分设计提供类比线索，但领域差距较大，需较多核查。
